Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

walker noun

baby walker

also baby walker

* our formation

B. Alex. 2 (Lewis & Short s.v. ambulātōrius)

* (our own formation) sella ambulātōria

baby walker

Our description: a seat that moves about. Ambulātōrius is said of machines moved to and fro, such as towers on wheels: aliās ambulātōriās … cōnfīxerant subjectīsque eās rotīs (B. Alex. 2). No ancient name for a baby walker is known, and Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini give none.

Examples

  • Vīn' tē in sellā ambulātōriā collocem?

    Shall I put you in your walker?composed

  • ēditus in lūcem jacuit sine vīribus īnfāns; mox quadrupēs rītūque tulit sua membra ferārum, paulātimque tremēns et nōndum poplite firmō cōnstitit adjūtīs aliquō cōnāmine nervīs

    born into the light, the baby lay without strength; soon he went on all fours like an animal, and little by little, wobbling, his knees not yet steady, he stood up, his muscles helped by some supportOv. Met. 15.221–224

See also baby, crawl, stand, pram.

SourcesLewis & Short: sella · Lewis & Short: ambulatorius · Lewis & Short: conamen

Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for a baby walker (searched under walker, baby walker, and Italian girello).

Bellum Alexandrinum checked against the Latin Library text (CLTK mirror); Ovid from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-ovidius), with Lewis & Short’s reading of cōnāmen here as “a support, prop”.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
